title: clade improvement-loop signal record
description: JSONL line schema for improvement-loop signal records emitted by shims, wrappers, git hooks, agent hooks, and manual entries. Every persisted record MUST validate; the validator enforces non-bypassable redaction. $defs.flow_envelope extends the same governance (same validator module, same non-bypassable redaction) to flow-spine events in .clade/flow/events.jsonl; it is a second record shape inside this one schema file, never a separate schema.

consumer_id.description: Stable id from registry/consumers.json. Digest aggregation resolves identity through the registry, never through local paths.

ts_utc.description: RFC3339 UTC timestamp. Local time is rendered only at display, never stored.

session_id.description: Source-specific session identifier (shim pid, agent session id, hook invocation id).

command_fingerprint.description: Normalized argv joined by ':' with stable ordering; user paths replaced by symbolic tokens. Used for cross-event grouping.

error_fingerprint.description: Normalized top stack frame, rule code, or error key. Empty failures use the literal string 'unknown'.

redaction_applied.description: Non-bypassable. The validator rejects records where this is false; there is no opt-out flag at any level.

flow_envelope.title: clade flow-spine event envelope
flow_envelope.description: Append-only event on the cross-substrate spine (.clade/flow/events.jsonl). Correlates work across pi / codex / herdr / work-loop through a shared work_id, with OTel-shaped span_id / parent_span. Validated by the same validator module and the same non-bypassable redaction as the signal record above.

work_id.description: W-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>, minted by the flow controller and by nothing else (plan section 3.2 rule 7). The control plane asks openWork for one rather than minting a second vocabulary; the slug is a mint seed, never an identity key. Null remains legal only for session_summary and validateFlowEvent enforces the biconditional.

parent_span.description: Parent span id, or null for a root span. Read from CLADE_FLOW_PARENT_SPAN when a dispatch runs inside another span.

phase.description: start/end pair one span; point is an instantaneous event (e.g. work.open). An unmatched start is an in-flight or stalled span, which is a reportable state, not a defect.

kind.description: OTel GenAI semconv gen_ai.operation.name vocabulary, plus work.open for the work-item lifecycle point event and decision.request for the human-decision queue. decision.request is a SPAN, not a point: phase=start is the question, phase=end is the answer, so an unanswered decision is an unclosed span and every in-flight / stalled query already covers it. There is deliberately no separate decision.resolve kind — it would be dead vocabulary that nothing reads, and the resolved-ness already lives in phase. Not OTel vocabulary; dotted like work.open to mark it as clade's own lifecycle, so an OTLP exporter maps it to a span event and NEVER to gen_ai.operation.name. It exists because the spine records what happened while nothing recorded what is waiting on a human — the \my contract states outright that pending decisions 'mostly exist only in the conversation', which no downstream can query. decision.clarify is a POINT event hanging off a decision.request span (parent_span = the decision), payload.direction = request | response — the back-and-forth on a question that was asked too tersely to answer. It is NOT the decision.resolve this same paragraph rules out: resolve would have restated a fact phase already carries, while a clarification is a fact nothing else records, and it deliberately does NOT close the span — the human still has to answer. Both halves share one kind because every reader wants them as one ordered list; two kinds would make the common query a union of two filters, and a reader that forgot one half would silently render half a conversation. decision.dismiss is also a POINT event, and it hangs off a span that ENDED blocked rather than off a decision.request: that is the one shape nothing could ever clear. A question closes by being answered, but a blocked span already has its end event — nothing can close it twice — so before this the only thing that removed a gated card was unrelated work starting in the same work id, and a question settled through another route sat on /decisions forever. NEVER a second end on the blocked span: the outcome records what happened, and overwriting it with what someone later decided about it would rewrite the history the spine exists to keep. payload.reason is required by the emitter for the same reason clarify carries text — a dismissal with no reason is indistinguishable from someone tidying the queue, which is the one thing it must not become. work.done / work.accept / work.drop / work.park are the work-item TERMINAL vocabulary, all POINT events carried on the work id itself: the spine could say a work item was in flight, failed, or quiet, but never that it was finished, and quiet is not done — settled is deliberately KEPT as the ambiguous state (nobody is moving and nobody claimed completion), so the claim had to get its own kind instead of overloading it. work.done is the one FAIL-CLOSED write on this stream: the emitter refuses it without payload.verification, because a lax done is worse than no done at all — it makes 'has this been accepted' rest on a fabricated 'is this finished'. work.accept and work.drop are the human terminal states and require payload.reason on the same basis `close --reason` does: a closure with no stated basis is a silent delete. work.park records that a work item stopped at a prose carrier (a HANDOFF section, a TD entry) waiting for a successor, so a reader sees 'parked at X' instead of an unexplained settled. work.reopened is the one event that UNDOES a work.done, and it exists because before it a done was final on this stream while the control plane's runtime had already put the work back in queued: a delivered work item whose requirement later moved, or whose receipts readiness judged insufficient, is running again, and a reader that saw only the standing work.done drew it as finished. A POINT event on the work id like every other work-level verdict, and deliberately NOT a second end or a retraction of the earlier one -- the done HAPPENED, and an append-only stream keeps it; what changed is that a later fact stands after it, so every reader asks which of done and reopened came last rather than whether a done exists. The emitter is fail-closed on payload.cause (revision | evidence_insufficient) and payload.reason on the same basis work.done is fail-closed on verification: the two causes are not interchangeable -- one says the requirement moved, the other says the record is short with the requirement standing -- and a reopen that cannot say which it is turns work.done into a claim anyone can silently retract. NEVER an end event on the work.open span: work.open is a point, and a work item is a fold over the whole stream rather than one long span. decision.revise and decision.pickup are POINT events hanging off a decision.request span, and they exist because an answer used to be final the moment it landed. decision.revise carries a replacement payload.answer (plus previous_answer and a revision counter): the human answered from a phone, then saw it was wrong. NEVER a second end on the decision span — the span already closed with what was decided at the time, and rewriting it would erase the very thing the spine keeps; the effective answer is therefore 'last revise, else the end payload', a read every consumer of an answer MUST use rather than reading the end alone. decision.pickup is the other half: an agent declaring it has read the answer and is acting on it, which is what makes a revision unsafe. Without it the only evidence of pickup is inference (a non-point, non-decision span starting in the same work id after the answer), and that inference is structurally blind to an agent that picked the answer up in a fresh process, where resolveWorkId mints an unrelated orphan work id. So pickup is the hard lock and the inference is the soft one, and a surface offering to edit an answer MUST say which of the two it is looking at. decision.amend is a POINT event hanging off a decision.request: it refreshes that question's rendered payload (options, recommended, wording) without closing or re-asking it, which is the only way an append-only spine can carry a parser fix back onto questions already on the queue. work.link is the work-item HIERARCHY point event, carried on the child work id with payload.parent_work_id naming its parent. An initiative or epic is NOT a new entity — it is an ordinary work item that other work items point at — so the hierarchy is the same shape as parent_span one level up, and no reader needs a second data model to draw it. Unlike work.open's first-origin-wins, re-parenting is deliberately LAST-WRITE-WINS: a work item is born once, but where it belongs is a judgement that changes. payload.parent_work_id may be null, and that is detach rather than a malformed event: without it 'no parent' would be reachable only at birth, and a mis-link with no correct parent to move to could never be undone on an append-only stream. The emitter is fail-closed on the KEY being present (null included) for the same reason work.done is fail-closed on verification — an event that names no parent records no fact and folds to a silent no-op. work.eta is the work-item DELIVERY-ESTIMATE point event, carried on the work id and LAST-WRITE-WINS like work.link, because an estimate is a judgement that changes rather than a fact recorded once. payload.target_ts is the estimated delivery date and payload.basis names where the number came from (human | agent-estimate); basis is REQUIRED because a bare date is indistinguishable from a template number, and an estimate that cannot show its own basis is the exact thing the estimate discipline forbids. There is deliberately NO derived-estimate kind: the fallback (a percentile over comparable finished work) is computed at fold time and NEVER written, because a derived value on an append-only stream is stale the moment the sample changes. Staleness is folded too, not stored -- a target_ts in the past on a work item that is not done reads as overdue, and NEVER as a future promise. dispatch.verdict is a POINT event carrying the patrol's verdict on a dispatch whose pane is gone -- abandoned, adjudicated, or reported -- onto the spine of the repo that dispatch named as its cwd. Before it, that verdict lived only in herdr-patrol's CLI output, so a dispatch that died without reporting was visible to whoever happened to run the patrol and to nobody else, which is the coverage boundary stall.ts documents. It is a point rather than a second end on the dispatch span for the same reason decision.dismiss is: that span may already have ended, and NEVER a second end -- the verdict records what a third party later determined, not what happened at the time. scenario.verdict.recorded is a POINT event carrying one BDD scenario's RED/GREEN/REFACTOR gate verdict (plan section 4.5), and the BDD evaluator is its SOLE writer (section 4.2): a scenario verdict written by the agent that wrote the scenario is not evidence, it is a claim, and section 7.5 exists precisely because the claim and the evidence diverge. It is a point rather than a span because a verdict is a judgement made after the run, not a period of time -- the run it judges is the reporter artifact's, and that artifact is referenced through payload.evidence_ids rather than re-timed here. The payload contract is docs/contracts/bdd/v1/scenario-verdict-event.schema.json: every section 4.5 payload field verbatim, plus scenario_id, because section 4.5 carries the scenario identity in an envelope stream_id that this envelope has no column for, and an identity-less verdict attaches to nothing. NEVER widen it with a veto list -- the anti_cheat flags are the machine-readable half and the full veto detail belongs in the evaluator's report, which is evidence rather than journal. The emitter is fail-closed on payload.gate_verdict, payload.phase and payload.scenario_id on the same basis work.done is fail-closed on verification: a verdict that cannot say what it judged, in which phase, or how it ruled records that somebody ran an evaluator, not what the evaluator concluded.

actor.description: Who acted: model slug, human id, or script name.

substrate.description: Execution substrate the span ran on. New substrates are added here, never by widening a payload field.

ts_utc.description: RFC3339 UTC. Local time is rendered only at display, never stored.

payload.description: Substrate-specific detail. Redaction recurses into it; nested values are redacted like top-level ones.

outcome.description: Settled result on a phase=end/point event; null while in flight (phase=start).

redaction_applied.description: Non-bypassable, same contract as the signal record: the validator rejects false; there is no opt-out at any level.

work_reopen_cause.title: clade work.reopened cause
work_reopen_cause.description: The two admissible reasons a delivered work item is running again (plan section 10.6 ruling (m)). A $defs of its own rather than a nested payload subschema, because the structural validator compiled from this file reads TOP-LEVEL properties only: a payload.cause enum written inside flow_envelope would be documentation the validator never executes. validateFlowEvent reads this list as a cross-field rule, and the flow emitter reads the same list, so `flow emit --kind work.reopened` with an unknown cause is refused at both doors. The runtime journal's REOPEN_CAUSES is a third copy that cannot import this one without pulling the signals module into the control-plane runtime; it is pinned equal by test instead.
